eips.title: Keyed Nonces for Frame Transactions
eips.summary: Toni noted the nonce field naming preference may require an update in EIP-8250.

moments.context: Toni said the leaning toward 'nonce' over 'nonce sequence' might need an update in 8250, and that he would check.

eips.title: Frame Transaction
eips.summary: Discussed adding a max fee field to Frame Transactions and whether gas accounting should remain in or be separated from this EIP.

moments.context: Lightclient identified three PRs for the next devnet, starting with the max fee PR that modifies the 8141 Frame Transaction fields.
Lightclient described the max fee update to 8141 as an aggregate cost field across execution, state, and blob gas dimensions.
Justin Florentine said he would consider proposing a PR to 8141 that removes gas accounting and falls back to status quo 8037, but lightclient objected.

eips.title: Unified multidimensional fee market
eips.summary: Debated whether its unified multidimensional fee market concepts should be integrated into Frame Transactions or kept separate.

moments.context: Lightclient explained the max fee PR originates from EIP-7999 and its goal of simplifying multi-dimensional gas UX for users.
Soispoke raised concerns that 7999 is complex and deserves more scrutiny before being shipped as a PR within frames.
Justin Florentine said he has always preferred 7999 over 8037 and suggested gas accounting should be pulled out of 8141 and handled by 7999 separately.
Lightclient asked whether 7999 was proposed for Hegota; Justin suggested removing gas accounting from 8141 and relying on 7999 instead.
Lightclient said since 7999 was not included in Hegota, someone should make a PR to frames showing what full 7999 integration would look like to compare against the max fee PR.

eips.title: State Creation Gas Cost Increase
eips.summary: Lightclient argued the state gas reservoir approach in 8037 is a hack for one-dimensional transactions and should not carry over to frames.

moments.context: Justin Florentine said 8037 was not nearly as simple as expected and preferred 7999's approach.
Lightclient said 8037 is a hack to make state gas work in a one-dimensional transaction object, and frames should expose the state gas field directly instead.

eips.title: Transaction Assertions via State Diff Opcode
eips.summary: Lightclient proposed removing the TXDIFF opcode from 7906 in favor of relying solely on TXTRACE; Alex Forshtat raised a pre-state use case against removal.

moments.context: Lightclient presented a PR to 7906 proposing removal of the TXDIFF opcode, arguing TXTRACE covers the same use cases and TXDIFF is just an optimization.
Alex Forshtat argued TXDIFF is needed for checking pre-state of storage slots, such as verifying a proxy's implementation slot was not front-run before the transaction.
Lightclient acknowledged the pre-state use case is valid and decided to table the PR and think about it further before merging.

moments.context: Ivan suggested adding SETCODEFROM and 8151 to bogota-devnet-2; lightclient agreed these are pretty critical parts of their PQ transition proposal.
